_comment: Context7 MCP - PINNED, read-only docs lookup. Audited 2026-08-17, see ops/TOOL_AUDIT_2026-08-17.md item 2.
_pin: Version is pinned exactly. Do NOT change 4.0.2 to @latest - that silently re-opens the supply chain.
_no_api_key: Intentionally NO apiKey / env block. Free tier works without one. Adding a key means an account, a credential on disk, and rate-limit tiers to manage - none of which this needs.
_egress_warning: Query text IS sent to context7.com. Context7's own schema says: do not include API keys, passwords, credentials, personal data, or proprietary code. Library names and generic topics only.
_tools: Server exposes exactly two read-only tools, verified by MCP handshake: resolve-library-id, query-docs. No write, shell, or filesystem tool exists in its surface.
_verification_status: Tool surface VERIFIED. Live doc lookup NOT VERIFIED - the audit container blocks context7.com. Re-run the smoke test on the Windows host before trusting it.
_smoke_test_on_windows: Expect on stderr: 'Context7 Documentation MCP Server v4.0.2 running on stdio'
Ctrl+C to exit. Then configure Codex and ask it to look up docs for a public library.
PASS = real documentation returned. FAIL = 'Error searching libraries: TypeError: fetch failed' (network/egress problem).
_rollback: Remove the context7 entry from the Codex MCP config. Optionally clear the npx cache. Nothing else persists.
